title: Upwork Monthly Hiring Insights: New AI developer roles emerge
summary: Upwork’s September hiring report shows AI video tops client searches as new AI developer roles emerge
body_markdown:
## AI video tops client searches as new AI developer roles emerge


“AI video” became the most-searched AI-related term on the Upwork Marketplace in September, while “AI SaaS developer” was the fastest-growing AI-related search year over year. Searches for “AI workflow automation,” “Agent developer,” "AI architect," and "AI integration" also grew rapidly. The data suggest that businesses are moving beyond general AI experimentation and becoming more precise about the people they need to put AI to work.


“In September, we saw businesses searching for specialists who can build AI-powered products, integrate AI into workflows, and turn AI-generated output into finished creative content,” said Jennifer Brett, managing director of the Upwork Research Institute. “The rise of AI SaaS developers, AI agent developers, and AI video creators shows how a more specialized workforce is emerging around AI implementation.”


## Hiring insights for September 2026


- **New AI roles are emerging as businesses move to development** . “AI SaaS developer” (a developer who builds AI capabilities into cloud-based software products) was the fastest-growing AI-related search year over year. “AI agent developer,” “AI architect,” and “Python AI developer” also ranked among the ten fastest-growing. This suggests businesses are increasingly looking for specialists who can turn AI capabilities into working products and software, not simply use existing AI tools.
- **AI video is creating demand across the production workflow.** “AI video” became the most-searched AI-related term in September, while “AI video creator,” “AI video generator,” and “AI video editor” all ranked among the top ten. “Video Editing Software” also grew both year over year and month over month. This suggests that more capable AI tools are not eliminating all video production work; they are creating demand for people who can[shape AI output](https://www.upwork.com/research/ai-generated-work-is-creating-more-work-for-humans) into finished video content.
- **AI implementation demand is showing staying power.** “AI Builder” recorded three consecutive months of contract growth, while “AI Implementation” and “AI Integration Deliverables” each grew for a second month. “AI workflow automation” was also the second-fastest-growing AI-related search year over year. The data suggest businesses continue to invest in the practical work required to embed AI into teams and workflows.


## Video and digital production lead September hiring momentum


The skills demand data below capture what Upwork Marketplace clients hired for in September compared with both September 2025 and August 2026. The quadrant chart highlights skills that are growing or declining year over year, while also showing whether demand accelerated or cooled month over month.


“WordPress Website Design” ranked first among skills growing both year over year and month over month, followed by “Video Editing Software” and “WordPress Customization”. The results point to continued investment in businesses’ digital presence, with demand spanning both website development and video production.


Video demand also remained above 2025 levels across “Corporate Video,” “Short Video Ad,” “Final Cut Pro,” and “AI Video Generation,” although these skills cooled month over month. Together, the findings show businesses hiring across the production workflow, from AI generation and editing to advertising and finished corporate content.

*Source: Upwork Marketplace data, September 2026 compared with September 2025 and August 2026*


#### General AI term loses ground as specialized roles emerge


“Data Scraping,” “API,” “Social Media Imagery,” “Education,” and “ChatGPT” declined both year over year and month over month in September.


The decline in “ChatGPT” contrasts with growing searches for more specialized AI roles and applications. Although one month cannot establish a definitive shift, the pattern may indicate that some clients are moving from general tool-based skills toward defined needs such as AI product development, automation, integration, and video production.


“Voice Acting,” “QuickBooks Online,” “Adobe Lightroom,” “Email Marketing Strategy,” and “Task Coordination” remained below year-earlier demand levels but recovered month over month.


#### AI hiring momentum extends from implementation to creative production


Persistent growth in skills demand shows that businesses are hiring across both the technical and creative sides of AI adoption. “AI Builder” recorded three consecutive months of demand growth, the longest streak in September, while “AI Implementation” and "AI Integration Deliverables” each grew for a second consecutive month.


Creative applications are showing momentum as well. “AI Ad Creation” and “AI Animation Tools” each recorded two consecutive months of growth. Together, these data points suggests businesses need talent not only to build and integrate AI systems, but also to apply them to finished marketing and creative work.


These remain early signals rather than established long-term trends, but their persistence reinforces the broader September finding that AI hiring is becoming more specialized but also connected to practical implementation.

## The AI Signal


### AI video becomes the most-searched AI term


“AI video” was the most-searched AI-related term on the Upwork Marketplace in September, moving ahead of “AI automation,” which led searches in[July](https://www.upwork.com/research/upwork-monthly-hiring-insights-july-2026) and[August](https://www.upwork.com/research/upwork-monthly-hiring-insights-august-2026) .


Video-related terms accounted for four of the ten highest-volume AI-related searches: “AI video,” “AI video creator,” “AI video generator,” and “AI video editor.” “AI developer,” “AI agent,” and “AI engineer” also ranked among the top ten, showing that clients are searching for both specific AI outcomes and the professionals needed to deliver them.


The prominence of AI video in both search and hired-contract data suggests demand is extending across distinct stages of production, from generation to editing and finishing content.


###### Figure 3: Top 10 AI-related search terms on the Upwork Marketplace, September 2026


*Source: Upwork Marketplace data, September 2026*


#### “AI SaaS developer” leads the rise in specialized AI roles


“AI SaaS developer” was the fastest-growing AI-related search in September compared with a year earlier. The search reflects demand for talent that can build complete AI-enabled software products or services, not simply apply AI within an isolated task.


The remainder of the ranking reveals two complementary areas of demand. Technical searches, including “AI workflow automation,” “AI agent developer,” “AI architect,” “AI integration,” and “Python AI developer,” show businesses seeking talent to build AI products and embed the technology into operating workflows. Creative searches, including “AI video creator,” “AI video ads,” “AI UGC,” and “AI video content creator,” show demand for specialists who can translate AI capabilities into finished creative content.


This extends a trend visible since[June](https://www.upwork.com/research/upwork-monthly-hiring-report-june-2026) : clients first became more specific about the outputs they wanted AI to produce and then about the people needed to deliver them. September’s data point to a further stage of specialization across product development, system implementation, and creative production.

## About the Upwork Monthly Hiring Insights Report


The Upwork Monthly Hiring Insights Report provides an early signal of broader shifts in how business leaders are hiring. It offers a complementary, more granular picture of trends in the U.S. labor market, with a focus on the independent talent economy.


### Methodology


**Skill demand quadrant methodology** Skills demand is measured by the number of distinct hired contracts whose job post mentions the skill in a given month, across U.S. marketplace clients. Each skill must meet minimum volume thresholds — at least 100 contracts in the current month and 50 in the comparison period. Year-over-year (YoY) change compares the current month's contract count to the same month one year prior. Month-over-month (MoM) change compares to the immediately preceding month. Skills are assigned to one of four quadrants based on the sign of each metric:


*Growing & Accelerating*


YoY Growth & MoM Growth — demand is higher than last year and still accelerating


*Growing & Cooling*


YoY Growth & MoM Decline — demand is higher than last year but cooling from a recent peak


*Declining & Recovering*


YoY Decline & MoM Growth — demand is lower than last year but showing short-term recovery


*Declining*


YoY Decline & MoM Decline — demand is lower than last year and continuing to decline


Within each quadrant, the top 5 skills are ranked by a composite score suited to the quadrant's character: for the top left and bottom right quadrants, skills are ranked by the sum of their YoY and MoM change to surface those with the strongest combined signal; for the top right, by YoY change alone (since MoM is negative by definition); and for the bottom left, by MoM change alone (since YoY is negative by definition).


**Demand persistence methodology** Demand persistence measures how many consecutive months a skill's hired contract count has increased, inclusive of the current month. A skill qualifies if it has at least 20 contracts in the current month and has gained at least 10 contracts in absolute terms over the duration of its streak. These lower thresholds (compared to the quadrant analysis) are intentional — persistent growth is most editorially interesting for emerging skills that have not yet reached mainstream volume. For the AI-specific persistence view, skills are further filtered to those matching a curated list of AI-related keywords.


**Search data** AI-related search terms were identified by matching raw client search queries against a curated AI-related keyword list. The volume ranking reflects total search occurrences within the month. The growth ranking measures year-over-year changes and compares current-month search counts against the same month one year prior, filtered to queries with at least 50 current-month and 20 prior-year occurrences to exclude low-volume noise.
